lab_title: Journey Through the Heart: Chambers, Valves, and the Path of Blood
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart and their relative positions
Identify the four valves of the heart and describe their function in preventing backflow
Identify the major vessels entering and leaving the heart
Trace the dual-loop pathway of blood through the pulmonary and systemic circuits
Explain why the left ventricle myocardium is thicker than the right ventricle myocardium
Correlate structural features of heart anatomy with functional roles in circulation

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the external anatomy of the heart and orient students to its position, orientation, and major surface landmarks before going inside.
key_visuals: A life-sized rotating 3D heart model floating in AR space
Labels highlighting anterior/posterior surfaces, apex, and base
Faint outlines of the great vessels emerging from the top of the heart
student_actions: Rotate and zoom the heart model to view it from multiple angles
Tap labeled hotspots to reveal the names of external landmarks
Answer a quick orientation quiz identifying apex vs base location

scenes.brief_purpose: Guide students to identify and differentiate the four chambers of the heart by cutting away the exterior wall to reveal internal structure.
key_visuals: A cutaway cross-section view of the heart exposing all four chambers
Color-coded highlighting distinguishing atria (thin-walled) from ventricles (thick-walled)
Semi-transparent overlay showing the septum dividing left and right sides
student_actions: Tap each chamber to reveal its name and a short description
Drag a slider to peel away the myocardium layer by layer
Complete a drag-and-drop labeling exercise placing chamber names on the model

scenes.brief_purpose: Show students the location and structure of the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves and explain their one-way function.
key_visuals: Close-up animated views of each valve opening and closing
Highlighted flaps/cusps of each valve with directional arrows showing blood flow
Side-by-side comparison of atrioventricular valves versus semilunar valves
student_actions: Tap each valve to trigger an open/close animation synced to a heartbeat sound
Predict which valve would leak if backflow occurred, using a simple selection tool
Match each valve to its correct chamber location in a short interactive check

scenes.brief_purpose: Identify the major vessels connecting to the heart and clarify which carry blood into versus out of the heart.
key_visuals: Highlighted vessels: superior and inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, and aorta
Color-coded flow arrows (blue for deoxygenated, red for oxygenated) at each vessel opening
Rotating view showing vessel entry/exit points relative to chambers
student_actions: Tap each vessel to see its name and whether it carries oxygenated or deoxygenated blood
Sort vessels into 'entering the heart' and 'leaving the heart' categories
Trace a finger along a vessel to preview where it leads before the full circulation scene

scenes.brief_purpose: Animate the full path of blood through the heart and body to help students understand the sequential dual-loop circuit.
key_visuals: An animated particle flow of blood moving through right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, lungs, pulmonary veins, left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and aorta
Color transition of particles from blue to red as blood passes through the lungs
A simplified schematic loop diagram displayed alongside the 3D heart for reference
student_actions: Play, pause, and step through the blood flow animation at their own pace
Tap each structure in the correct order to test recall of the circulation pathway
Answer a sequencing question arranging chambers/valves/vessels in correct blood flow order

scenes.scene_name: Why the Left Ventricle is Thicker
scenes.brief_purpose: Help students connect structure to function by comparing the myocardial thickness of the left and right ventricles and relating it to workload.
key_visuals: Side-by-side cross-sections comparing right ventricle wall thickness to left ventricle wall thickness
Overlay showing pressure differences between pulmonary and systemic circuits
Visual metaphor animation showing the left ventricle pumping blood across a much longer distance (whole body) versus the right ventricle pumping a short distance (lungs)
student_actions: Measure and compare wall thickness using an in-app virtual caliper tool
Answer a conceptual question explaining why the left ventricle needs more muscular force
Reflect via short written response on how this relates to conditions like left ventricular hypertrophy

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate learning by having students independently identify structures and narrate the full path of blood without guided prompts.
key_visuals: The complete, unlabeled 3D heart model available for free exploration
An interactive checklist tracking which structures have been correctly identified
A final animated playback of the full circulation pathway with valve sounds synced to a heartbeat
student_actions: Label all chambers, valves, and vessels from memory using tap-to-label interactions
Narrate or select the correct sequence of blood flow through the entire heart
Complete a final assessment quiz covering structure identification and functional reasoning
